title: Blazhko periods of field RRab stars are not stable clocks: 24% of 635 change within 3 years of ZTF data, and 47% of 228 change between LINEAR (2002-2008) and ZTF (2018-2025)
abstract: Question: Is the Blazhko modulation period P_B of RR Lyrae stars a stable clock, as a rotation (oblique pulsator) model requires, and are P_B changes tied to pulsation-period changes? Approach: We fitted pulsation harmonics with a period derivative plus modulation triplets to ZTF DR24 g/r light curves (2018-2025) of 1,989 LINEAR RRab stars, including 179 RRab of the Donev & Ivezic (2025) Blazhko list. A blind scan found modulation with P_B 8-400 d in 638 stars. We refitted the two ZTF halves (median separation 3.2 yr) and searched LINEAR data (2002-2008) within +-25 percent of the ZTF modulation frequency. A LINEAR detection needs F >= 14.2, the 99th percentile of 1,836 null trials on unmodulated stars. Errors were calibrated with 5,104 constant-P_B simulations (night-wise wild bootstrap); formal errors are 1.48 (ZTF) and 1.77 (LINEAR) times too small. Results: Within ZTF, 24.1 percent of 635 stars change P_B at 3 calibrated sigma (null 2.9 percent) and 12.8 percent at 5 sigma (null 1.9 percent). From LINEAR to ZTF (16 yr), 46.9 percent of 228 stars change at 3 sigma and 29.4 percent at 5 sigma (null 4.9 percent). The median significant change is 2.2 percent in 3 yr and 4.4 percent in 16 yr. The noise-corrected rms change grows by a factor 1.56 (95 percent: 1.15-2.18) from 3.2 to 16 yr: less than a random walk (2.24) and much less than a drift (5.0). Relative P_B changes are about 540 times the relative pulsation-period changes. Modulated stars change their pulsation frequency more than 459 unmodulated stars (median 1.4e-5 against 6.2e-6 c/d; p = 1e-23). The change of the modulation frequency has no overall correlation with the change of the pulsation frequency (Spearman +0.07); only stars with a dominant f0-f_m side peak show a positive relation (+0.41, p = 0.002, n = 52), and a fixed side-peak beat model fails on size. Limitations: LINEAR has about 70 nights per star, so only 238 stars have LINEAR P_B and changes above 25 percent are not tested; annual aliases and peak swaps remain possible; RRc stars and P_B outside 8-400 d are not tested. display.caption: Fraction of modulated RRab stars with a change of the modulation frequency f_m above a given calibrated significance (blue), against 5,104 simulations with a constant modulation period (grey). Left: ZTF first half against second half (635 stars, median 3.2 yr). Right: LINEAR 2002-2008 against ZTF 2018-2025 (228 stars, median 16 yr). Dotted lines: 3 and 5 sigma.

Change of the modulation frequency against change of the pulsation frequency, LINEAR to ZTF, for stars with a significant f0 change. Left: the side peak at f0+f_m is larger. Right: the side peak at f0-f_m is larger. Dashed and dotted lines: a beat with a fixed nonradial mode at the dominant side peak would put the stars on the line with slope -1 (left) or +1 (right). The changes of f_m are about 4 times too large for this model.

Change of the pulsation frequency from LINEAR (2002-2008) to ZTF (2018-2025) for 637 modulated and 459 unmodulated RRab stars. Modulated stars change their pulsation frequency more (20 percent against 3 percent above 5e-5 c/d).

citations.reason: Donev & Ivezic (2025, AJ 169, 310): LINEAR+ZTF Blazhko star list; we use its identifiers. Its tabulated Blazhko-peak periods often fall near the lunar month or half year and agree with our P_B for 5 of 112 stars, so they cannot measure P_B changes.
Sesar et al. (2011): LINEAR photometric survey, source of the 2002-2008 light curves.
Palaversa et al. (2013): LINEAR periodic variable classification (RRab sample).
astroML data repository: distribution of the LINEAR light curves and catalogues.
Bellm et al. (2019): Zwicky Transient Facility.
Masci et al. (2019): ZTF data system and light curves.
Stothers (2006): variable convective driver; permits P_B changes, consistent with our result but not uniquely.
Buchler & Kollath (2011): 9:2 resonance model; detuning changes can change P_B.
Nowakowski & Dziembowski (2001): resonant nonradial modes. If the nonradial mode frequency is fixed, f_m changes should equal +-f0 changes; observed f_m changes are about 4 times larger.
LaCluyze et al. (2004): Blazhko and pulsation period changes of XZ Cyg (anticorrelated).
Le Borgne et al. (2012): GEOS RR Lyr long-term Blazhko and pulsation timing; P_B changes in individual stars. Our population result agrees.
Jurcsik et al. (2009): Konkoly Blazhko Survey, context for modulation properties.
Campaign study of ZTF period changes of Cepheids with an independent Gaia epoch; related survey timing method for pulsating stars.
